name: The hollow verb (ajwaf)
definition: A verb whose middle root letter is wāw or yāʾ, such as qāla (q-w-l) and bāʿa (b-y-ʿ); called 'hollow' because its middle is empty of a sound letter.
body: In the past the weak middle letter becomes alif (qāla, bāʿa); in the present it shows as a long vowel (yaqūlu, yabīʿu); in the imperative and the jussive, when the last letter is silent, it drops (qul). The active participle puts a hamza in its place (qāʾil). The books also call it dhū al-thalātha, 'the one of three', since its first-person past has three letters (qultu).

examples.text: qāʾil, the active participle: hamza in place of the wāw.
